caveats:
Each ZIP download contains the original scanned TIFF files for a single calendar
year, including monthly and dekadal scans. The files are provided in a ZIP archive
to preserve the original sources and may be extracted and converted as needed.


The accuracy of SPI is entirely dependent on the quality and length of the historical
rainfall record used for the baseline. In regions with sparse gauge networks, interpolation
errors in the input precipitation data can propagate into the SPI calculation. SPI
does not account for temperature or evapotranspiration, only rainfall.
dataset_source: African Center of Meteorological Applications for Development (ACMAD)
methodology_other:
SPI is calculated by fitting a probability distribution (usually Gamma) to long-term
precipitation records and then transforming that distribution into a normal distribution.
Negative values indicate dry conditions (drought), while positive values indicate
wet conditions. The magnitude of the negative value corresponds to the severity
of the drought (e.g., -1.5 is severe drought, -2.0 is extreme).
name: acmad-standardized-precipitation-index
notes:
The Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI) is the globally recommended standard for
characterizing meteorological drought. It quantifies observed precipitation as a
standardized deviation from the long-term probability distribution function for
a specific location and time scale. This dataset typically includes multiple time-scales
(e.g., 1-month, 3-month, 6-month, 12-month) to capture different types of drought impacts,
from immediate soil moisture deficits to long-term hydrological stress.


Because SPI is normalized, it allows for safe comparisons between different climatic
zones—allowing a wet region and a dry region to be compared on the same scale of
drought severity.

organization.title: African Center of Meteorological Applications for Development
organization.description:
ACMAD was created through **Resolution 540** of the **UNECA Conference of Ministers** in **April 1985**, following the severe droughts of the 1970s and 1980s, **ACMAD** was established in **Niamey, Niger** in **October 1992** with two mandates: - **Continental Weather and Climate Watch Centre for Africa** Monitoring, forecasting, and early warning for droughts, floods, tropical cyclones, and other extreme events. In this regard, ACMAD became: + The Continental Climate Watch Centre was achieved with ACMAD designated by the WMO Congress after a successful demonstration phase as a Regional Climate Centre for Africa in May 2015. + The Continental Weather Watch Centre was achieved with the Continental Multi-Hazards Advisory Centre inaugurated in November 2022, and ACMAD is providing contributions to continental watches and disaster situation reports to support the situation room operations at the African Union Commission Headquarters in Addis Ababa. - **Institution of excellence for the application of meteorology for sustainable development** This includes capacity building, development of methods, tools and products, contributions to global weather and climate programs, database development, and research and innovation as functions. Since **July 2024**, ACMAD has been a member of the **NoE (Africa Network of Excellence for DRR)**. **ACMAD Provides the following Bulletins with Continental coverage:**
  • Impact-based Forecast Bulletin
  • Multi-Hazard Bulletin
  • Seasonal Climate Forecast Bulletin
  • Monthly Climate Bulletin
The bulletins are in PDF format and are are available on the website: https://www.acmad.org * API for the Drought: https://ada.acmad.org/api
